issue.title: task-status-hooks doc claims the Cancel row and reconcile apply the same canceled-link cleanup, but reconcile also removes struck links and whole mixed-prose bullets

task_type_fields.impact: Readers and agents implementing new cancel paths, such as the proposed relation cancel labels, are told the immediate prune and reconcile are equivalent. That leads to wrong parity tests and to surprise when reconcile later removes text the immediate cancel kept. Docs-only fix: state that reconcile's cleanup is broader (whole list-item subtree, struck forms included) and is the eventual state, or align the algorithms in a separate decision.
task_type_fields.repro:
Read docs/task-status-hooks.md "Canceled Task References" (bob-cli 50f6c91b, lines ~145-190).

- Lines 157-161 say reconcile removes the *complete list item* for a canceled link, including "exactly struck forms", authored prose, and sibling links on that item.
- Lines 184-189 say the Ctrl+Shift+P Cancel row uses deferral-prune dedicated-bullet/token semantics (mixed prose loses only the token), then claim "Struck links, closed Pomodoros, and other days' notes are untouched either way" and that reconcile "re-derives the same cleanup on its next run".

The nav implementation matches lines 184-187: `planDeferredPomodoroLinkCleanup` in bob-plugins `bob-navigation-hotkeys/src/540-plugin-decay-picker-and-cancel.js` (`applyTaskCancelFromEditor`). Reconcile matches lines 157-161: the cancelled-reference loop in `src/native/task_status_hooks/structure.rs`. So reconcile can later delete a struck link, or a whole mixed-prose bullet, that the immediate cancel deliberately kept. That is not "the same cleanup".

issue.creation_reason: Found while verifying the relation cancel-labels research: the doc's parity claim contradicts its own reconcile rule and the nav implementation, which would mislead the parity tests for the new cancel path.
